google.hebrewNote: Google's own pages may open in English.

intro.body1: The agent creates events in your own calendar. For that it needs a free key that belongs to you.
intro.body2: Five short steps on Google's site, about five minutes. You can also do this later.
intro.privacy: The agent reads the busy and free times of your calendar and creates only the events you approved.

step1.i1: Open the Google Cloud console and create a new project. Any name will do.
step1.i2: With that project selected, open the Google Calendar API page and press Enable.
step1.tip: If a page asks you to choose an organisation, choose No organisation.
step1.title: Create a project

step2.i1: Open the OAuth consent screen and choose External.
step2.i2: Fill in an app name and your own email address, then save.
step2.i3: On the Audience page press Publish app, so that the sign-in does not expire after seven days.
step2.testingBody: In Testing mode Google signs you out after seven days, and the agent asks you to connect again.
step2.testingTitle: What happens if I leave it in Testing?
step2.title: Set up the consent screen

step3.i1: Open Credentials, press Create credentials, then OAuth client ID.
step3.i2: For Application type choose Desktop app - not Web application.
step3.i3: Use the name below, so you recognise it later.
step3.title: Create the key

step4.drop: Drop the JSON file you downloaded here
step4.hint: The file stays where it is - only its contents are read.
step4.title: Add the key file

step5.firewall: Windows may ask whether this app can use the network - Cancel or Allow both work.
step5.title: Sign in
step5.unverified: Google will say it has not verified this app. That is expected: the app is yours and you are its only user. Choose Advanced, then Go to (your app name).
